title: MCP in 2026: Specification Updates and Ecosystem Growth
content:
## Overview

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard — originally developed by Anthropic and now maintained with broad community participation — that defines how AI models communicate with external tools, data sources, and services. Since its launch in late 2024, the ecosystem has grown from ~20 reference implementations to over 5,000 community-maintained servers by mid-2026. A major specification revision is finalized on July 28, 2026.

---

## Ecosystem Scale

| Period | Estimated public MCP servers |
|---|---|
| Late 2024 (launch) | ~20 reference implementations |
| Early 2026 | 500+ |
| Mid-2026 | 5,000+ |

The official registry at [registry.modelcontextprotocol.io](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/) is the canonical index for discovering and publishing servers. The community adds new servers every week.

### Server Categories (Mid-2026)

- **Databases:** PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis
- **File storage:** Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, Amazon S3
- **Version control:** GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket
- **Project management:** Jira, Asana, Linear, Notion
- **Communication:** Slack, email, Discord, Microsoft Teams
- **Web / browser:** Playwright/Puppeteer automation, web scraping
- **Dev infrastructure:** Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines
- **Finance:** Stripe, Plaid, QuickBooks

---

## 2026 Specification (RC → Final July 28, 2026)

A release candidate for the next major MCP spec version was published in mid-2026. The final version ships on **July 28, 2026**. Key changes:

### Stateless Protocol Core

The spec now formally defines a stateless transport mode. MCP servers can be deployed as plain HTTP endpoints with no session state, making serverless (Lambda, Cloudflare Workers) and edge deployments practical without requiring long-lived connections.

### Extensions Framework

A structured mechanism for servers to declare optional capability extensions. MCP clients that don't support a given extension degrade gracefully rather than failing, greatly improving cross-client interoperability. Extensions are declared in the server manifest and versioned independently of the core spec.

### Tasks

A new first-class protocol primitive for long-running operations. Tasks give clients a way to start an operation asynchronously, poll for status and streaming progress events, and receive a typed result. This directly addresses a gap that emerged as agents began triggering operations (web crawls, code runs, file conversions) that take seconds or minutes to complete.

### MCP Apps

A packaging format that bundles a server definition, OAuth configuration, permission scopes, and optional UI metadata into a single distributable unit — analogous to browser extensions. Users can install an MCP App from the registry and it becomes available across any MCP-capable client. Addresses the friction of manually configuring servers in each tool.

### Authorization Hardening

- OAuth 2.1 flows required (OAuth 2.0 deprecated)
- PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) mandatory for all authorization code flows
- Explicit token scoping guidance to reduce over-permissioned community servers
- Clearer rules on token storage and rotation

### Formal Deprecation Policy

The spec now includes an explicit versioning and deprecation schedule. Protocol features move through `current → deprecated → removed` with a minimum 12-month window between deprecated and removed. Server authors can plan upgrades without unexpected breakage.

---

## MCP and Claude

Claude natively supports MCP across all its surfaces:

- **Claude Code:** MCP servers are configured in `.claude/settings.json` and are available to all agents in the session. The Claude Code web and desktop apps ship with built-in MCP integrations (GitHub, Slack, Google Drive, and others) that users connect via OAuth.
- **Claude API:** Clients pass MCP server configurations in the API request body; Claude calls their tools automatically as part of tool use.
- **Claude.ai:** A curated set of MCP-backed integrations is available via the claude.ai interface.

---

## Building MCP Servers

The reference implementation and community server collection live at [github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers). Official SDKs are available for TypeScript, Python, Kotlin, Go, and Rust.

Every MCP server exposes one or more of three primitive types:

- **Tools** — callable functions with typed JSON Schema inputs and outputs; by far the most common primitive
- **Resources** — readable data sources the model can fetch on demand (files, DB rows, API responses)
- **Prompts** — reusable prompt templates with typed arguments, enabling standardized workflows across clients

Before writing a new server, check the registry and the GitHub repo — given 5,000+ existing servers, the integration you need likely already exists.
